source_text: תְּ֭רֹעֵ/ם בְּ/שֵׁ֣בֶט בַּרְזֶ֑ל כִּ/כְלִ֖י יוֹצֵ֣ר תְּנַפְּצֵֽ/ם׃
english_snapshot: You will break them[a] with an iron scepter[b]; like a potter’s vessel you will shatter them.

signals.text: An alternative vocalization, reflected in some ancient versions and echoed in Revelation, gives “You will shepherd them” or “You will rule them.” The WLC pointing and the parallel “you will shatter them” support “break them” here.

source_text: מִ/פִּ֤י עֽוֹלְלִ֨ים וְֽ/יֹנְקִים֮ יִסַּ֪דְתָּ֫ עֹ֥ז לְמַ֥עַן צוֹרְרֶ֑י/ךָ לְ/הַשְׁבִּ֥ית א֝וֹיֵ֗ב וּ/מִתְנַקֵּֽם׀׃
english_snapshot: From the mouths of infants and nursing babies you have established strength[a] because of your foes, to stop the enemy and the avenger.

signals.text: Or “praise,” following the Septuagint tradition reflected in Matthew 21:16; the Hebrew text reads “strength.”

source_text: וַ/תְּחַסְּרֵ֣/הוּ מְּ֭עַט מֵ/אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְ/כָב֖וֹד וְ/הָדָ֣ר תְּעַטְּרֵֽ/הוּ׃
english_snapshot: Yet you made him a little lower than God[a], and crowned him with glory and honor.

signals.text: Or 'than heavenly beings'; the Septuagint reads 'than angels,' a rendering reflected in Hebrews 2:7.

source_text: אַ֭שֻּׁרֵי/נוּ עַתָּ֣ה סבבו/ני עֵינֵי/הֶ֥ם יָ֝שִׁ֗יתוּ לִ/נְט֥וֹת בָּ/אָֽרֶץ׃
english_snapshot: At every step they now surround me[a]; they fix their eyes to bring me down to the ground.

signals.text: The Hebrew shifts from 'our steps' to 'they surround me.' 'At every step' expresses the setting while retaining the singular object of the verb.

source_text: מגדל יְשׁוּע֪וֹת מַ֫לְכּ֥/וֹ וְ/עֹ֤שֶׂה חֶ֨סֶד לִ/מְשִׁיח֗/וֹ לְ/דָוִ֥ד וּ/לְ/זַרְע֗/וֹ עַד עוֹלָֽם׀־׃
english_snapshot: He makes his king’s victories great and shows steadfast love to his anointed[a], to David and his offspring forever.[b]

signals.text: The consonantal form can also be read, “a tower of deliverances for his king.”

source_text: כִּ֥י סְבָב֗וּ/נִי כְּלָ֫בִ֥ים עֲדַ֣ת מְ֭רֵעִים הִקִּיפ֑וּ/נִי כָּ֝/אֲרִ֗י יָדַ֥/י וְ/רַגְלָֽ/י׃
english_snapshot: For dogs have surrounded me; a company of evildoers has encircled me; like a lion—my hands and my feet.[a]

signals.text: The Masoretic Hebrew reads “like a lion—my hands and my feet,” a difficult expression. The Greek reads “they dug my hands and feet,” often rendered “they pierced.” A Hebrew scroll from Nahal Hever is transcribed with a different spelling, ka'aru, but its meaning and the earliest wording remain disputed.

source_text: נְקִ֥י כַפַּ֗יִם וּֽ/בַר לֵ֫בָ֥ב אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא נָשָׂ֣א לַ/שָּׁ֣וְא נַפְשִׁ֑/י וְ/לֹ֖א נִשְׁבַּ֣ע לְ/מִרְמָֽה־׀־׃
english_snapshot: The one who has clean hands and a pure heart, who has not set his heart on falsehood[a] or sworn deceitfully.

signals.text: The written Hebrew text reads “my soul”; the traditional reading is “his soul.” The phrase means setting one’s desire or inner self on falsehood; “falsehood” may also mean what is empty or worthless, and some understand it as an idol.

source_text: זֶ֭ה דּ֣וֹר דרש/ו מְבַקְשֵׁ֨י פָנֶ֖י/ךָ יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
english_snapshot: Such is the generation of those who seek him, who seek your face, O God of Jacob.[a] Selah

signals.text: The Hebrew is difficult and has simply “Jacob” after “your face”; it may identify the seekers as Jacob. Some ancient versions read “God of Jacob.”

source_text: הִבִּ֣יטוּ אֵלָ֣י/ו וְ/נָהָ֑רוּ וּ֝/פְנֵי/הֶ֗ם אַל יֶחְפָּֽרוּ־׃
english_snapshot: They looked to him[a] and were radiant[b], and their faces will never be put to shame.

signals.text: The written text has “to me,” while the traditional reading is “to him.”

source_text: כִּ֤י יְהוָ֨ה אֹ֘הֵ֤ב מִשְׁפָּ֗ט וְ/לֹא יַעֲזֹ֣ב אֶת חֲ֭סִידָי/ו לְ/עוֹלָ֣ם נִשְׁמָ֑רוּ וְ/זֶ֖רַע רְשָׁעִ֣ים נִכְרָֽת׀־־׃
english_snapshot: For Yahweh loves justice and does not forsake his faithful ones; they are preserved forever,[a] but the offspring of the wicked will be cut off.

signals.text: The ancient Greek and Syriac add, “but the lawless will be driven away forever.”

source_text: זֶ֤בַח וּ/מִנְחָ֨ה לֹֽא חָפַ֗צְתָּ אָ֭זְנַיִם כָּרִ֣יתָ לִּ֑/י עוֹלָ֥ה וַ֝/חֲטָאָ֗ה לֹ֣א שָׁאָֽלְתָּ׀־׃
english_snapshot: Sacrifice and offering[a] you did not desire; ears you have opened for me[b]; burnt offering and sin offering you did not ask for.

signals.text: Hebrew: “ears you have dug for me,” likely an idiom for enabling hearing or obedience. The Septuagint, followed in Hebrews 10:5, reads “a body you prepared for me.”

source_text: קִרְבָּ֤/ם בָּתֵּ֨י/מוֹ לְֽ/עוֹלָ֗ם מִ֭שְׁכְּנֹתָ/ם לְ/דֹ֣ר וָ/דֹ֑ר קָֽרְא֥וּ בִ֝/שְׁמוֹתָ֗/ם עֲלֵ֣י אֲדָמֽוֹת׀׃
english_snapshot: Their inward thought is that their houses will last forever, their dwelling places from generation to generation; they name lands after themselves.[a]

signals.text: An alternative textual reading is: “Their graves are their houses forever, their dwelling places from generation to generation.”

source_text: ישימות עָלֵ֗י/מוֹ יֵרְד֣וּ שְׁא֣וֹל חַיִּ֑ים כִּֽי רָע֖וֹת בִּ/מְגוּרָ֣/ם בְּ/קִרְבָּֽ/ם־׃
english_snapshot: Let death come upon them[a]; let them go down alive to Sheol, for evil is in their dwelling[b][c][d], in their midst.

signals.text: Or, 'Let desolations come upon them,' 'May death come suddenly upon them,' or similar. The Hebrew of the opening word is difficult, and the exact nuance is uncertain.

source_text: הַֽ/אֻמְנָ֗ם אֵ֣לֶם צֶ֭דֶק תְּדַבֵּר֑וּ/ן מֵישָׁרִ֥ים תִּ֝שְׁפְּט֗וּ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָֽם׃
english_snapshot: Do you indeed speak righteousness, O silent ones?[a] Do you judge uprightly, sons of man?[b]

signals.text: Hebrew אֵלֶם is difficult. The Masoretic Text points it as a form related to silence or muteness; another vocalization yields “mighty ones” or “gods”: “Do you indeed speak righteousness, O mighty ones?”

source_text: אֱלֹהֵ֣י חסד/ו יְקַדְּמֵ֑/נִי אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים יַרְאֵ֥/נִי בְ/שֹׁרְרָֽ/י׃
english_snapshot: My God, in his steadfast love[a], will go before me; God will let me look on my enemies.

signals.text: The written text can be rendered 'God, in his steadfast love.' The reading tradition supports 'my God of steadfast love.'

source_text: לְ֭מַעַן יֵחָלְצ֣וּ/ן יְדִידֶ֑י/ךָ הוֹשִׁ֖יעָ/ה יְמִֽינְ/ךָ֣ ו/ענ/נו׃
english_snapshot: So that your beloved ones may be delivered[b], save with your right hand and answer us.[a]

signals.text: Some construals read the final plea as 'and answer me' rather than 'and answer us.'

source_text: מוֹאָ֤ב סִ֬יר רַחְצִ֗/י עַל אֱ֭דוֹם אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ נַעֲלִ֑/י עָ֝לַ֗/י פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת הִתְרֹעָֽעִֽי׀־׃
english_snapshot: Moab is my washbasin[a]; on Edom I cast my sandal; over me, O Philistia, shout in triumph[b]!

signals.text: The Masoretic form is a feminine imperative addressed to Philistia. Many translations instead read, 'Over Philistia I shout in triumph.'

source_text: יְהִֽי שֻׁלְחָנָ֣/ם לִ/פְנֵי/הֶ֣ם לְ/פָ֑ח וְ/לִ/שְׁלוֹמִ֥ים לְ/מוֹקֵֽשׁ־׃
english_snapshot: May their table before them become a trap, and when they are at peace, let it become a snare[a].

signals.text: Or 'and for their well-being, a snare.' The Masoretic Hebrew refers to peace or welfare, not explicitly to peace offerings.

source_text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הראית/נו צָר֥וֹת רַבּ֗וֹת וְ/רָ֫ע֥וֹת תָּשׁ֥וּב תחיי/נו וּֽ/מִ/תְּהֹמ֥וֹת הָ֝/אָ֗רֶץ תָּשׁ֥וּב תַּעֲלֵֽ/נִי׀׃
english_snapshot: You, who have made us see many troubles and calamities[a], will revive us again[b]; from the depths of the earth you will bring me up again[c].

signals.text: The Hebrew shifts from 'us' here to 'me' in the next colon.

source_text: אַתָּ֣ה רִ֭צַּצְתָּ רָאשֵׁ֣י לִוְיָתָ֑ן תִּתְּנֶ֥/נּוּ מַ֝אֲכָ֗ל לְ/עָ֣ם לְ/צִיִּֽים׃
english_snapshot: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; you gave him as food to the desert creatures.[a]

signals.text: The Hebrew phrase is difficult; it may refer to desert creatures, a people inhabiting the desert, or desert dwellers.

source_text: כִּֽי חֲמַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם תּוֹדֶ֑/ךָּ שְׁאֵרִ֖ית חֵמֹ֣ת תַּחְגֹּֽר־׃
english_snapshot: For human wrath will praise you; you will gird yourself with the remaining wrath.[a]

signals.text: The Hebrew phrase is difficult. The main text follows the Masoretic wording and preserves its image of girding oneself with the wrath that remains.

source_text: אָ֤ז דִּבַּ֥רְתָּֽ בְ/חָ֡זוֹן לַֽ/חֲסִידֶ֗י/ךָ וַ/תֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁוִּ֣יתִי עֵ֭זֶר עַל גִּבּ֑וֹר הֲרִימ֖וֹתִי בָח֣וּר מֵ/עָֽם־־׃
english_snapshot: Then you spoke in a vision to your faithful ones[a] and said, “I have bestowed help on a mighty one[b]; I have raised up a young man from among the people.”

signals.text: Some ancient versions read “your faithful one.”

source_text: כִּֽי אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה מַחְסִ֑/י עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן שַׂ֣מְתָּ מְעוֹנֶֽ/ךָ־׃
english_snapshot: For you have made Yahweh—my refuge, the Most High—your dwelling place[a].

signals.text: The Masoretic Hebrew is compressed and allows more than one construal. Or preserve its abrupt shift of voice: 'For you, Yahweh, are my refuge; you have made the Most High your dwelling place.' The main text does not add a verb meaning 'said,' which is absent from the Masoretic text.

source_text: דְּע֗וּ כִּֽי יְהוָה֮ ה֤וּא אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים הֽוּא עָ֭שָׂ/נוּ ו/לא אֲנַ֑חְנוּ עַ֝מּ֗/וֹ וְ/צֹ֣אן מַרְעִיתֽ/וֹ־־׃
english_snapshot: Know that Yahweh is God. He made us, and we did not make ourselves[a]; we are his people and the sheep of his pasture.

signals.text: Or, following the traditional marginal reading, “He made us, and we are his.”

source_text: עִנָּ֖ה בַ/דֶּ֥רֶךְ כח/ו קִצַּ֥ר יָמָֽ/י׃
english_snapshot: He weakened my strength[a] on the way[b]; he shortened my days.

signals.text: The Ketiv, the written text, reads 'his strength'; the Qere, the Masoretic reading tradition, reads 'my strength.'

source_text: שָׁרַ֣ץ אַרְצָ֣/ם צְפַרְדְּעִ֑ים בְּ֝/חַדְרֵ֗י מַלְכֵי/הֶֽם׃
english_snapshot: Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings.[a]

signals.text: Hebrew “their kings.” The singular “their king” appears in the Exodus plague narrative, but the psalm uses the plural form here, perhaps poetically or collectively.

source_text: ידעת כִּֽי יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְ֭הוָה דִּ֣ין עָנִ֑י מִ֝שְׁפַּ֗ט אֶבְיֹנִֽים־׃
english_snapshot: I know[b] that Yahweh will uphold the cause of the afflicted[a] and secure justice for the needy.

signals.text: The written Hebrew form is normally read “you know,” but the Masoretic scribal reading tradition gives “I know,” which fits this concluding confession.

source_text: חַסְדִּ֥/י וּ/מְצוּדָתִ/י֮ מִשְׂגַּבִּ֪/י וּֽ/מְפַלְטִ֫/י לִ֥/י מָ֭גִנִּ/י וּ/ב֣/וֹ חָסִ֑יתִי הָ/רוֹדֵ֖ד עַמִּ֣/י תַחְתָּֽ/י׃
english_snapshot: My steadfast love and my fortress, my stronghold and my deliverer, my shield, in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.[a]

signals.text: Some ancient versions read “peoples” instead of “my people.”

source_text: מַֽלְכוּתְ/ךָ֗ מַלְכ֥וּת כָּל עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וּ֝/מֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּ/ךָ֗ בְּ/כָל דּ֥וֹר וָ/דֽוֹר־־׃
english_snapshot: Your kingdom is a kingdom for all ages[a], and your dominion is throughout every generation.[b]

signals.text: The Masoretic Text lacks a line beginning with nun in this alphabetic psalm. The Hebrew scroll 11Q5 adds here: 'God is faithful in his words and loyal in all his deeds.' The standard Greek text has a corresponding line with 'the Lord' instead of 'God.' The line's inclusion and exact wording remain disputed; the main text here follows the Masoretic Text.

source_text: צַדִּ֣יק יְ֭הוָה בְּ/כָל דְּרָכָ֑י/ו וְ֝/חָסִ֗יד בְּ/כָל מַעֲשָֽׂי/ו־־׃
english_snapshot: Yahweh is righteous in all his ways and faithful in all his works[a].

signals.text: Or 'kind' or 'gracious'; some translations read 'holy' here, reflecting a different textual tradition than the Masoretic Text's 'faithful/steadfast' sense.
